free_tier.stated: Pay as you go includes USD 12 in credit each month per organization, covering 3,000 minutes on a 2-vCPU Linux x86 runner; the credit renews monthly and unused credit does not carry over.
free_tier.notes: The credit is measured on a 2 vCPU Linux x86 runner at USD 0.002 a minute; a larger machine draws it down faster in proportion to its per-minute rate. An organization gets the allowance only when none of its admins administers another organization receiving it.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a VM with a disk, not a stored object; no per-object size limit is published for sandboxes

retention.stated: A sandbox disk survives a pause for 7 days after its time limit ends and is then deleted with the disk; sandboxes that cannot pause are deleted with their disk at the limit, and agent sandboxes are deleted when the session ends.

egress.terms: Networking is included in the price without separate bandwidth metering; published HTTPS ports are metered at 500 requests a second per URL, with bursts up to 1,000, then 429; Git Mirroring outbound data is USD 0.15 per GB and that charge is separate from sandboxes.

interface_detail: The avr CLI creates, connects and deletes sandboxes over SSH, with a REST API at api.avrea.com for creation and deletion, an SSH terminal and remote desktop in the console, and published HTTPS URLs for ports; remote desktop tunnels through SSH.
tooling: the avr CLI installed from Homebrew, Go, PyPI or GitHub releases, an SSH client, editor remote extensions, and a browser for the console; scp and rsync work through the generated SSH config.
chaining: A coding agent or CI job creates a VM from a repository and branch, reuses the organization's build caches, and forks a paused Linux x86 sandbox for a parallel task; any published HTTPS URL is public to whoever holds it, so apps using it need their own authentication.

limits.value: without a payment method a sandbox runs at most 2 hours from creation, extensions included; the default is 2 hours and the organization is capped at 64 vCPUs at once and 256 queued jobs
with a payment method the default time limit is 8 hours, maximum 7 days, and a paused sandbox is deleted with its disk 7 days after its time limit ended
macOS sandboxes require a 24-hour minimum reservation, then bill at the same per-minute rate
a published HTTPS URL accepts 500 requests a second with bursts to 1,000, then 429, and up to 1,000 open requests, then 503; up to 10 ports may be published
an account that is not an organization admin can keep 2 sandboxes at a time and cannot set egress rules; macOS sandboxes are enabled by contacting Avrea

limits_note: Sandbox compute bills at the published runner rates, from USD 0.002 a minute for 1 vCPU and 4 GB Linux x86 to USD 0.08 a minute for 8 vCPU and 24 GB macOS; sandboxes bill for reserved time by the second.
binding_note: The credit covers 3,000 minutes on the smallest runner, but a sandbox without a payment method ends after 2 hours from creation with no extension, so the clock caps a long agent task before the credit runs out.

identity_cost.detail: The CLI sign-in prints a link and code to approve in a browser, and the console sign-in creates or selects an organization; a card is added in Settings > Billing to get the 8-hour sandbox limit, and the information-for-consumers page states payment is made online by payment card. The sign-up form itself was not entered, so any further fields are unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: Sandboxes that cannot pause are deleted with their disk at the time limit; a paused sandbox is deleted after 7 days, agent sandbox disks are discarded at session end, and forwarded tokens stored on a disk are copied into forks.
confidence_note: The price, credit and macOS reservation minimum come from the provider pricing page read 2026-11-24; the time limits and retention come from the sandbox and billing docs, egress from the provider blog and HTTPS docs, and the sign-in and payment gate from the CLI docs and consumer information page.
